A metal box. Health spending up sixty-eight percent.
Ever save for something, and the money just leaks away?
In rural Kenya, researchers worked with savings groups: seven hundred seventy-one people.
Some got a simple metal box. A slot, a padlock, and the key.
Others got the same box. But an officer kept the key.
A year later, the keep-your-key box raised preventive health spending about sixty-eight percent.
And the box they couldn't open?
Naming the money was enough. Locking it too tight hurt in emergencies.
So give your savings a box and a name. And keep the key.
